examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Exponent for a Matrix With Distinct Real Eigenvalues
examples.problem:
Find $e^{At}$ for ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14058518/assets/bf972d6172dc5282be366a87138ac9088216484082251482383de605c720b568.png) 

*Hint: The eigenvalues of $A$ are $1$ and $4.$*
examples.worked_solution:
We have a square matrix of dimension $n=2.$ Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{At} & ={\alpha }_{1}At+{\alpha }_{0}I \\  & ={\alpha }_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}]t+{\alpha }_{0}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & 0 \\ -3{\alpha }_{1}t & 4{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_0$ are functions to be determined.

Consider the polynomial $r(\lambda) = \alpha_1 \lambda + \alpha_0.$ The eigenvalues of $At$ are 

$$
\lambda_1=t, \qquad
\lambda_2=4t,
$$

both of multiplicity one. Thus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}r(t)={e}^{t} \\ r(4t)={e}^{4t}\end{aligned}\,⇒\,{\begin{aligned}t{\alpha }_{1}+{\alpha }_{0}={e}^{t} \\ 4t{\alpha }_{1}+{\alpha }_{0}={e}^{4t}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system for $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_0{:}$

- Subtracting the first equation from the second one, we get

$$
3t\alpha_1 = e^{4t} - e^{t}
\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
\alpha_1 = \dfrac{1}{3t}\bigl(e^{4t}-e^{t}\bigr).
$$

- Multiplying the first equation by $4$ and subtracting the second one, we get

$$
3\alpha_0 = 4e^{t} - e^{4t}
\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
\alpha_0 = \dfrac{1}{3}\bigl(4e^{t}-e^{4t}\bigr).
$$

Substituting $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_0$ into the expressions for the entries of $e^{At},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & =(\frac{1}{3t}({e}^{4t}-{e}^{t}))t+\frac{1}{3}(4{e}^{t}-{e}^{4t}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}({e}^{4t}-{e}^{t}+4{e}^{t}-{e}^{4t}) \\  & ={e}^{t} \\ -3{\alpha }_{1}t & =-3(\frac{1}{3t}({e}^{4t}-{e}^{t}))t \\  & ={e}^{t}-{e}^{4t} \\ 4{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & =4(\frac{1}{3t}({e}^{4t}-{e}^{t}))t+\frac{1}{3}(4{e}^{t}-{e}^{4t}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}((4{e}^{4t}-4{e}^{t})+(4{e}^{t}-{e}^{4t})) \\  & ={e}^{4t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,
